uncited: It serves as a critical reference for implementers to understand the failure modes and resource constraints inherent in diffusion-guided NeRF editing, distinguishing these issues from the algorithmic mechanics described in [RePaint-NeRF](14365-repaint-nerf.md).

detail: supported
In such cases, the edit may be incomplete, failing to fully replace the original geometry [S1].

The claim states that edits may be incomplete, failing to fully replace original geometry. Source [S1] explicitly mentions in the 'Limitations' section that 'in some cases, especially the new object shape is hugely different from the old one, the training process will be very tough for the model (see Fig. 3, the cup from the hotdog is not completely changed).' This directly supports the claim that edits can be incomplete and fail to fully replace the original geometry.

Generating a high-quality 3D model at the object level requires more than 30 minutes of optimization [S1].

The claim states that generating a high-quality 3D model at the object level requires more than 30 minutes of optimization. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states: 'it still takes more than 30 minutes to generate a relatively highquality 3D model at the object level.' This directly supports the claim.
supported
RePaint-NeRF was proposed by the authors of [S1] to enable NeRF editing via semantic masks and diffusion model guidance.

The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states in the Conclusion section that the authors proposed a 'NeRF editing framework based on the pre-trained 2D diffusion model guidance.' It further details that the method obtains the edited scene by 'regenerating the masked part through the gradient guidance of the diffusion model' and mentions 'semantic mask acquisition.' This aligns perfectly with the claim that RePaint-NeRF (the method described) was proposed to enable NeRF editing via semantic masks and diffusion model guidance.
supported
RePaint-NeRF is both time and memory intensive [S1].

The claim states that RePaint-NeRF is time and memory intensive. The evidence explicitly states in the notes and the passage that 'the whole process is time-consuming and space-consuming' and 'it still takes more than 30 minutes to generate a relatively highquality 3D model'. 'Space-consuming' in this context refers to memory usage. Therefore, every fact in the claim is supported by the evidence.
supported
Geometric artifacts arise when restricted view angles are used during optimization [S1].

The claim states that geometric artifacts arise when restricted view angles are used during optimization. Source [S1] explicitly notes in its bullet points that 'Restricted view angles cause geometric artifacts at image edges' and describes in the passages how 'angle constraint will influence the shape of the generation,' citing an example where a generated object at the edge combines features from multiple sources incorrectly. This directly supports the claim.
supported
Due to these resource demands, the method cannot scale to larger resolutions or larger scenes [S1].

The claim states that the method cannot scale to larger resolutions or larger scenes due to resource demands. Source [S1] explicitly states in the 'Limitations' section: 'The first and most obvious problem with our method is that the whole process is time-consuming and space-consuming. For this reason, we cannot extend to a larger resolution of data or a larger scene.' This directly supports the claim.
supported
Objects generated at the periphery of the view may incorrectly combine features from multiple source objects, whereas central regions remain consistent [S1].

The claim states that objects at the periphery may incorrectly combine features from multiple source objects, while central regions remain consistent. Source [S1] explicitly mentions in its notes and passages that 'generated objects at the periphery may incorrectly combine features from multiple source objects' and provides an example where 'the generated daisy on the edge of the view is actually combined by two orchids, while the generated daisy in the central location is much more normal.' This directly supports every part of the claim.
supported

This article documents the empirical limitations of the RePaint-NeRF method [S1], specifically regarding computational efficiency, geometric fidelity under significant shape changes, and view-angle consistency.

The claim accurately reflects the limitations described in Source [S1]. The source explicitly states the method is 'time-consuming and space-consuming' (supporting 'computational efficiency'), notes that training is 'very tough' when the 'new object shape is hugely different from the old one' (supporting 'geometric fidelity under significant shape changes'), and mentions that 'angle constraint will influence the shape of the generation' with examples of artifacts at edges (supporting 'view-angle consistency').
supported

The limitations described herein were identified during the evaluation of this framework, which uses gradient guidance from a pre-trained 2D diffusion model to regenerate masked parts of the scene [S1].

The claim accurately reflects the content of the provided evidence. The evidence explicitly states in the Conclusion that the method uses 'gradient guidance of the diffusion model' from a 'pre-trained 2D diffusion model' to regenerate masked parts. It also details the limitations in the Limitations section, noting that the process is 'time-consuming' (taking >30 minutes), struggles when shapes differ drastically, and has issues with restricted view angles causing artifacts. All specific facts mentioned in the claim are present in the evidence.
supported
